label: Custom token with an explicit fee-hook boundary
summary: Add explicitly reviewed token behavior while keeping any generic project fee-hook mechanics explicit and policy neutral.
requiredFacts: Exact token-side behavior across transfer, mint, burn, balance and allowance paths
Why the behavior belongs in the token rather than a PoolManager callback
Canonical PoolKey and exact generic hook or no-hook behavior selected by project intent
Gross and net token balance behavior across swaps, liquidity, claims, exits and integrations
Every token authority, parameter bound, exemption, rescue path and retirement rule
requiredFiles: Any explicitly selected generic hook source binding
Cross-contract threat model and test plan
requiredTests: Token behavior matrix across ordinary transfers, swaps, liquidity, claims and exits
Any explicitly selected generic fee behavior is correct in every exposed swap quadrant
Pool settlement and router behavior use exact observed token balance deltas
Authority, parameter-bound, exemption, pause, rescue and retirement adversarial cases
Token liabilities and any project fee-hook liabilities remain isolated and solvent
risks: Token-side behavior can break pool settlement or integrations regardless of hook selection
Mutable token controls can create hidden confiscation, transfer blocking or economic changes
Blurring token and hook responsibilities can hide value flows or double charge users
